/config settings panel: tab row, rounded ╭─╮ search box, scrolling list, key-hint footer The generic menu grammar finds its region top by walking up from the footer for the nearest rule or box border within REGION_SCAN_WINDOW (30 rows, menu.ts). Here that rule is the search box's ╰─╯ bottom border: 24 rows above the footer at 82 columns, and 32 above it on a 120-column live capture (2026-09-22), whose taller list fits 30 setting rows between the two. Past the window the walk finds nothing, detectMenuRegion returns null, and the screen falls to the unread-dialog card instead. A fix has to stop measuring the region top in a fixed row count — size the window to the pane's own height, or anchor on the panel's tab row rather than the nearest rule — and it must still decline a borderless buffer, which is what the bound is there for.
entries.knownKeyGap: The footer names 'Enter/↓ to select' as ONE compound token, and menuKeyFor takes a single key token, so Enter and Down are dropped and the menu offers Up and Escape alone. Candidate grammar: a compound-token reader for key-hint footers, which the '↑/↓' form of the same hint needs too.

entries.knownKeyGap: The /resume grammar (resume.ts, ADR 0058) lifts each session as a row whose tap walks the pointer and sends Enter, plus the footer's Esc row. PromptModel has no place for footer actions, so Ctrl+A, Ctrl+B and Ctrl+R stay on the Keys drawer, and with the pointer on the top row no tap needs Up.

entries.knownRaw: The last non-blank line is 'Esc to cancel', ONE segment, and parseKeyHintFooter needs at least two, so the generic menu never sees a footer to claim. Candidate grammar: a single-hint footer variant of the generic menu. Widening the two-segment floor is not free: that floor is what keeps an ordinary statusline from reading as a modal.
